Repo: C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Windows paths, Git-Bash/PowerShell environment). Kodely, an AI website builder. No new npm dependencies allowed.

CONTEXT — read fully first:
- lib/site-records.ts — specifically `recordSavedReply()` and the create flow around it. Right now, when a `SiteRecord` is created via `POST /__records/<kind>`, a raw manage-link token is shown ONCE in the same-origin HTML response page. If the submitted fields contain a plausible email address (checked via `STRICT_EMAIL_RE`, now exported from lib/site-endpoint.ts), the reply currently just states in text that no auto-email is sent yet. Your job: actually send that email.
- lib/mail.ts — the existing mail-sending wrapper (`sendMail`, `isMailConfigured`) used everywhere else in this codebase.
- lib/site-forms.ts — read `notifyOwner()` and `submissionEmail()` fully as your pattern reference: same escaping discipline (`escapeHtml`), same `headerSafe()` header-injection guard, plain-text + HTML alternative, "best effort, always" semantics (never block or fail the main request if the email send fails), and the `EMAIL_MAX_PER_HOUR`-style per-project cap that already exists there to stop a form flood from becoming a mail flood.

THE IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM site-forms.ts's EXISTING EMAIL: that one notifies the PROJECT OWNER (a known, trusted address already on file in the User table). This new one sends to an ARBITRARY ADDRESS TYPED INTO A PUBLIC FORM BY WHOEVER SUBMITTED IT. That is a real abuse surface distinct from anything already built: without care, this becomes a way to make Kodely's mail server send email to any address a stranger picks (spam relay / harassment vector — "someone keeps getting emails from a Kodely site they never visited because an attacker keeps typing their address into a booking form"). Design against this specifically:

1. **Strict, separate rate limiting on this send path**, independent of (in addition to) the existing record-creation rate limits: cap how many of these visitor-confirmation emails can go out per project per hour AND per exact-recipient-address per hour (so even a project under its normal creation-rate-limit can't be used to spam one specific victim address repeatedly). Reuse `lib/site-endpoint.ts`'s existing rate-limiting building blocks (e.g. `createBurstLimiter`) rather than inventing new machinery — read what's already there before adding anything.
2. **Fixed, minimal, non-reflective email content.** The email must NOT echo arbitrary submitted field values verbatim as free text that could be crafted to look like phishing bait. It should say, plainly and factually: which published site (project name — already public, since only published sites can receive submissions), which `kind` of record, that a manage-link was requested/created, and the link itself. Do not include the record's other field values in the email body. Everything interpolated (project name, kind) must go through the exact same `escapeHtml`/`headerSafe` discipline already used in site-forms.ts.
3. **No reply-to set to anything.** Unlike `notifyOwner()` (which sets reply-to to the visitor's address so the OWNER can reply), this email goes TO the visitor — there is no reason to invite a reply, and the `From` must stay Kodely's own sending address exactly as `sendMail()` already enforces elsewhere (never derived from anything user-submitted).
4. **Never block the main response on this.** Exactly like `notifyOwner()`: fire-and-forget, `void sendMail(...).catch(...)`, logged on failure, never awaited by the request handler, never changes what the visitor sees in the same-origin reply page (the reply page's own text can still mention "we've also emailed this link to the address you gave us" — but only state that if the send was actually attempted, not if it was skipped by a rate limit or `isMailConfigured()` being false).
5. **Skip silently and honestly if `isMailConfigured()` is false** — same as everywhere else in this codebase; the HTML reply's wording must not claim an email was sent if it wasn't.

Also update the same-origin reply text in `recordSavedReply()` to accurately reflect the new real behavior instead of the current "no auto-email is sent yet" placeholder — say plainly whether an email is going out or not, and never claim something happened that didn't (e.g. if the per-recipient rate limit is hit and the email is skipped for that reason, the reply must not falsely say it was sent).

STEPS:
1. Read lib/site-records.ts, lib/site-forms.ts, lib/site-endpoint.ts, and lib/mail.ts in full before writing anything.
2. Implement the confirmation email exactly as scoped above, with the two-axis rate limiting (per-project AND per-recipient-address).
3. Update the reply page's wording to be accurate in every case (sent / not sent because mail isn't configured / not sent because rate-limited).
4. Run `cd /c/Users/edmem/kodely-prod && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0` — both must be completely clean before you finish.

Note: a separate agent will start immediately after you finish, working on a real visitor-accounts primitive that ALSO touches lib/site-records.ts's create flow. Keep your changes to the specific functions you need (the reply generation and the new email-sending logic) rather than a broad refactor of that file, so the next agent's diff against your version stays easy to reason about.

Report back: the exact rate-limit numbers you chose and why, the email's exact content, and confirmation both checks passed clean.
